<b>Носоглотка</b> — верхний отдел, позад: Nasopharynx — the upper part, behind the choanae and above the soft palate. It carries air only: during swallowing the soft palate seals it off. On its roof lies the pharyngeal tonsil (adenoids); on its side walls open the auditory tubes, which equalize pressure in the middle ear.
<b>Ротоглотка</b> — от мягкого нёба до в: Oropharynx — from the soft palate to the upper edge of the epiglottis, behind the root of the tongue. Both air and food pass through it — this is where their paths cross. The palatine tonsils sit on its side walls between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches; the lingual tonsil covers the root of the tongue.
<b>Гортаноглотка</b> — позади гортани, о: Laryngopharynx — behind the larynx, from the epiglottis to the lower edge of the cricoid cartilage (level of the 6th cervical vertebra), where the pharynx becomes the esophagus. In front is the laryngeal inlet; on either side of it are the piriform recesses, which channel food down into the esophagus.
<b>Верхний констриктор</b> начинается от: Superior constrictor arises from the pterygoid hamulus, the pterygomandibular raphe and the mandible. Its fibers curve around the pharynx and meet behind it at the midline raphe. When it contracts, it narrows the upper pharynx and draws its wall toward the soft palate.
<b>Средний констриктор</b> веером начина: Middle constrictor fans out from the horns of the hyoid bone: its upper fibers rise, its lower fibers descend, and on the outside it overlaps the lower edge of the superior constrictor. Behind, all its fibers insert into the pharyngeal raphe.
<b>Продольные мышцы</b> — шилоглоточная,: Longitudinal muscles — stylopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus and salpingopharyngeus. Stylopharyngeus runs down from the styloid process, passes between the superior and middle constrictors and blends into the wall and the thyroid cartilage. During swallowing these muscles shorten the pharynx and raise the larynx.
<b>Ротовая фаза</b> — произвольная. Конч: Oral phase — voluntary. The tip of the tongue presses against the palate, and a wave of tongue contraction from front to back squeezes the bolus toward the back of the mouth (the fauces). As soon as the bolus touches the root of the tongue and the tonsillar pillars, receptors trigger the reflex — from then on, swallowing runs by itself.
<b>Глотка</b> — мышечная трубка длиной 1: The pharynx is a muscular tube 12–14 cm long, running from the skull base to the 6th cervical vertebra. In front it opens into the nasal cavity, the mouth and the larynx, so it is divided into the naso-, oro- and laryngopharynx. In the oropharynx the paths of air and food cross. Choose a region.
<b>Перекрёст путей.</b> Воздух (голубой): Where the paths cross. Air (blue) flows from the nose through the nasopharynx and oropharynx forward into the larynx and trachea. Food (orange) goes from the mouth backward into the laryngopharynx and the esophagus, which lies behind the trachea. The paths cross in the oropharynx, so breathing pauses for an instant during each swallow.
Глотка — перекрёсток: через неё идут и в: The pharynx is a crossroads: both air and food pass through it. In the single second a swallow takes, the soft palate seals off the nose and the epiglottis the larynx, breathing stops, and three constrictor muscles push the bolus into the esophagus in a wave.
<b>Глоточная фаза</b> — рефлекторная, ≈: Pharyngeal phase — reflexive, ≈ 0.5 s. The soft palate rises and closes off the nasopharynx; the larynx and hyoid move up and forward, the epiglottis folds down over the laryngeal inlet, the vocal folds close — breathing stops. The upper esophageal sphincter relaxes, and the constrictors drive the bolus down toward it in a wave.
<b>Пищеводная фаза.</b> Комок проходит ч: Esophageal phase. The bolus passes through the open upper esophageal sphincter, which closes behind it. A peristaltic wave carries the bolus to the stomach in 8–10 s. The palate, epiglottis and larynx return to their places — breathing resumes.
<b>Нижний констриктор</b> — самый толсты: Inferior constrictor is the thickest. Its thyropharyngeal part runs from the thyroid cartilage obliquely up to the raphe. The cricopharyngeal part arises from the cricoid cartilage; its fibers run almost horizontally, encircle the pharynx like a ring and stay closed at rest — this is the upper esophageal sphincter. Killian’s triangle lies between the two parts at the back.
<b>Мышцы глотки.</b> Снаружи — три конст: Pharyngeal muscles. Outside are three constrictors nested inside one another like a stack of cups: the inferior overlaps the middle, the middle overlaps the superior. Inside are the longitudinal muscles. Nerve supply: cranial nerves IX and X via the pharyngeal plexus (stylopharyngeus — IX alone). Turn on “Wave” or choose a muscle; the back view hides the spine.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The pharynx is a muscular tube behind the nasal cavity, the mouth and the larynx. Its wall consists of mucosa, a fibrous layer (the pharyngobasilar fascia) and muscle: three constrictors outside and longitudinal muscles inside. Behind it lie the loose retropharyngeal space and the prevertebral muscles.

The entrance to the pharynx is ringed by Waldeyer’s lymphoid ring: the pharyngeal and tubal tonsils above, the palatine tonsils at the sides, the lingual tonsil below. They are the first to meet microbes from air and food.

How it works

We swallow 500–1000 times a day, including during sleep. The oral phase is voluntary; the pharyngeal and esophageal phases are reflexive: the swallowing center in the medulla switches the muscles on in sequence and briefly shuts off inhalation.

Four “gates” keep food out of the nose and larynx: the soft palate, the epiglottis, the aryepiglottic folds and the closed vocal folds. Lifting the larynx up under the root of the tongue adds protection and opens the upper esophageal sphincter.

Medicine

  • Dysphagia — impaired swallowing after a stroke, in Parkinson’s disease and myasthenia gravis; dangerous because of aspiration — food entering the airway — and pneumonia.
  • Adenoids — an enlarged pharyngeal tonsil in children: blocked nasal breathing, snoring, ear infections when the auditory tube openings are covered.
  • Tonsillitis — inflammation of the palatine tonsils; a peritonsillar abscess pushes the uvula toward the healthy side.
  • Zenker’s diverticulum — an outpouching of mucosa through Killian’s triangle above the cricopharyngeal part: regurgitation of undigested food, bad breath.
  • The Heimlich maneuver — when a piece of food blocks the larynx, abdominal thrusts just below the rib cage expel it with a burst of air from the lungs.

Conventions

  • Modes 1 and 3 show a schematic midline section of the head and neck (right half, seen from inside): tissues are simplified and the mucosa is not shown in full; the side wall of the lumen is a dark backdrop, and the tonsil, the tube opening and the nasal conchae on it are drawn without perspective; the nasal septum is removed. The section stops at the skull base, and the face and neck profile is schematic.
  • Mode 2: the spine is removed, and the skull is translucent with its vault cut away; the muscles are thin sheets on a schematic pharyngeal tube, and palatopharyngeus and salpingopharyngeus inside are not shown.
  • Swallowing is slowed about fourfold; movements of the palate, tongue, larynx and epiglottis are averaged, the bolus shape and size are schematic, and the piriform recesses (where the bolus flows around the laryngeal inlet) are not shown.
